project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence: Root cause sink: src/main/java/net/lingala/zip4j/unzip/UnzipEngine.java, method getOutputStream(String outPath, String newFileName) (lines 416-437), fed by getOutputFileNameWithPath(String outPath, String newFileName) (lines 439-447) which does `return outPath + System.getProperty("file.separator") + fileName;` with zero validation. Trust boundary: `fileName` ultimately comes from `fileHeader.getFileName()` / a caller-supplied `newFileName`, and fileHeader.getFileName() is populated directly from the zip's local/central directory record by HeaderReader.java (readFileHeader / readLocalFileHeader, around lines 314-330 and 929-941) with no path-traversal filtering — i.e., fully attacker-controlled data from an untrusted zip file crossing into filesystem operations. Distinct sinks sharing this same tainted `file` object that a complete fix must guard (all reachable from the single unsanitized path built at line 422, matching the alert's traces): (1) line 424-425 `file.getParentFile().mkdirs()` — arbitrary directory creation at attacker-chosen path; (2) line 428-429 `file.exists()` / `file.delete()` — arbitrary existing-file deletion/overwrite at attacker-chosen path; (3) line 432 `new FileOutputStream(file)` — arbitrary file write/content injection at attacker-chosen path. A 4th related, not-separately-alerted but same-class sink is line 93 in unzipFile(): `UnzipUtil.applyFileAttributes(fileHeader, new File(getOutputFileNameWithPath(outPath, newFileName)), unzipParameters)`, which re-derives the same unsanitized path and applies file attributes to it post-extraction — a complete fix should centralize the containment check in getOutputFileNameWithPath/getOutputStream so this call site is covered too. My POV exercises all three primary sinks (mkdirs, delete, FileOutputStream) in one extractAll() call because they all execute sequentially against the same malicious `file` inside getOutputStream when the traversal entry is processed.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: Running the POV against the unpatched code creates /tmp/zip4j_zipslip_pov/evil_marker.txt (two directory levels ABOVE the requested extraction destination /tmp/zip4j_zipslip_pov/extracted/sub) containing the marker string "ZIP4J_POV_PWNED", and ZipFile#extractAll completes without throwing. The POV process prints "VULNERABLE: ..." and exits with status 0. On a correctly patched build, extraction must either throw/refuse to extract the traversal entry or write it only inside the destination directory, so the escaped marker file is never created and the POV exits non-zero.
parsed_output.notes: The alert lists three "vulnerabilities" whose traces all converge on the same source (getOutputFileNameWithPath at line 422) and the same tainted `file` object, diverging only in which downstream sink consumes it (line 432 FileOutputStream write; line 425 getParentFile()+mkdirs; line 429 exists()+delete()). Since all three sinks sit in the same 20-line method (getOutputStream) and are triggered together during any real extraction of a traversal entry, I built one POV targeting the shared root cause (unsanitized concatenation in getOutputFileNameWithPath) via the public ZipFile#extractAll API — this single run exercises all three sinks in sequence (mkdirs escapes the root, delete/exists checks the escaped path, and the final FileOutputStream write lands the attacker's content outside destPath), rather than writing three near-duplicate POVs. I verified both directions: exit 0 on the current vulnerable UnzipEngine.java, and exit 1 after temporarily adding a canonical-path containment check to getOutputStream (change reverted after verification — working tree is clean except for the new .security-pipeline/pov/ files and the untracked target/ build directory).
parsed_output.regression_hint: Invariant a correct fix must enforce: for every archive entry, the canonical (resolved) path of the computed output File must be equal to, or a descendant of, the canonical path of the caller-supplied extraction root (outPath) — checked BEFORE any of mkdirs(), delete(), or FileOutputStream creation happens, ideally centralized in getOutputFileNameWithPath/getOutputStream so both getOutputStream (lines 422-432) and the applyFileAttributes call site (line 93, which calls getOutputFileNameWithPath again) are covered by one check. If the check fails, extraction of that entry must be aborted with an exception rather than silently truncating/re-rooting the name. Known bypass variants the fix must also block, not just plain "../": (1) mixed/absolute traversal like "/etc/passwd" or "C:\\..." (fileName used as-is, no leading-separator check); (2) backslash-based traversal on the write path itself if fileName contains "..\\" (Zip4jUtil.decodeFileName / getOutputFileNameWithPath just appends System.getProperty("file.separator") without normalizing internal separators); (3) deeply nested "..%2f.."-style or repeated "../../../.." sequences beyond the depth used in this POV; (4) traversal via the `newFileName` parameter path (ZipFile.extractFile(fileHeader, destPath, unzipParameters, newFileName) lets a caller-supplied newFileName reach the same unsanitized concatenation — should be validated identically to fileHeader.getFileName()); (5) symlink-based escapes if the extraction root itself contains a pre-existing symlink pointing outside — canonicalization (getCanonicalPath) rather than simple string-prefix checks on the raw path is needed to catch this; (6) zero-length/empty path segments or trailing-dot tricks that some canonicalizers normalize differently across platforms — verify the containment check runs after canonicalization on both sides.
parsed_output.summary: Created a real POV (Zip4jZipSlipPov.java) that crafts a malicious zip archive with a path-traversal entry name ("../../evil_marker.txt") and extracts it through zip4j's public API (net.lingala.zip4j.core.ZipFile#extractAll), which routes through Unzip -> UnzipEngine.unzipFile -> UnzipEngine.getOutputStream -> getOutputFileNameWithPath. The unsanitized concatenation of the caller's destination path with the attacker-controlled fileHeader.getFileName() lets the extracted file escape the intended extraction root, confirming the CWE-022 Zip Slip vulnerability. Verified the command exits 0 on the current (vulnerable) code and exits 1 when a canonical-path containment check is added to getOutputStream (simulated patch, then reverted).

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root cause: net.lingala.zip4j.unzip.UnzipEngine#getOutputFileNameWithPath() built the extraction target by naive string concatenation of the caller's outPath with the attacker-controlled entry name (fileHeader.getFileName() or a caller-supplied newFileName), with no check that the result stayed inside outPath. That single unsanitized path fed three sinks in getOutputStream() (parent-dir mkdirs, exists()/delete(), and the FileOutputStream write) as well as the applyFileAttributes call site in unzipFile() (line 93), all named in the alert's traces.

Fix: added a new static helper, Zip4jUtil.checkPathIsContainedInRoot(rootPath, entryOutputPath, entryName), that resolves both the extraction root and the candidate output path with File#getCanonicalPath() (which normalizes "..", mixed separators, and resolves symlinks) and throws a ZipException unless the candidate is the root itself or a canonical descendant of it. This is invoked once inside UnzipEngine#getOutputFileNameWithPath(), so every caller of that method — the getOutputStream() write path and the applyFileAttributes call — is covered by one check, matching all three "vulnerabilities" entries in the alert (mkdirs, delete/overwrite, FileOutputStream write) and both traversal encodings shown (with/without the intermediate `file` variable in the trace).

Also hardened the two sibling call sites in net.lingala.zip4j.unzip.Unzip.java that build the same class of unsanitized path outside of UnzipEngine and were not covered by the above fix: the directory-entry mkdirs() branch in initExtractFile() (fileHeader.isDirectory() == true, which never reaches UnzipEngine) and checkOutputDirectoryStructure()'s parent-directory mkdirs() for file entries (which runs before UnzipEngine.unzipFile() and would otherwise still create arbitrary escaped directories even though the subsequent file write would later be blocked). Both now call the same Zip4jUtil.checkPathIsContainedInRoot() helper before touching the filesystem.

This blocks: relative "../" traversal at any depth, traversal via a caller-supplied newFileName (same helper, same trust boundary), and symlinked-root escapes (canonicalization resolves existing symlinks). Absolute-path entries are already contained by the pre-existing string-concatenation behavior (outPath + separator + fileName lexically nests under outPath) and are additionally caught by the canonical-path check as a defense-in-depth measure.

Regression coverage: added src/test/java/net/lingala/zip4j/ZipSlipRegressionTest.java, a dependency-free (no JUnit is wired into this pom.xml) class with a main() method that (1) builds a zip with a ".." traversal file entry and asserts extraction throws and no file lands outside the destination, (2) does the same for a ".." traversal directory entry (covering the Unzip.java fix), and (3) extracts a normal nested-path zip and asserts it still succeeds and lands in the right place, guarding against over-restrictive regressions. Verified: build succeeds (mvn -B -DskipTests package), the provided POV script (.security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh) now exits 1 / "NOT VULNERABLE" against the patched build (was exit 0 / "VULNERABLE" before), and the new regression class prints PASS for all three checks.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Behavioral change: extraction of any archive entry whose resolved path would land outside the destination directory now throws ZipException instead of silently writing/deleting outside the root — this is the intended fix but is a breaking behavior change for any (unusual) caller that relied on the old traversal-permissive behavior. getCanonicalPath() does I/O (resolves the real filesystem path) and can itself throw IOException, which is wrapped into ZipException; on filesystems/paths where canonicalization behaves unexpectedly (e.g. certain network mounts) this could in theory reject a legitimate path, though this is the standard, widely-used mitigation pattern for zip-slip (e.g. same approach used by many other libraries). No dependency or build-config changes were made. The new test file is plain Java (no JUnit) since the project's pom.xml has no test framework dependency; mvn test still succeeds (surefire finds the *Test-named class but runs 0 tests since it has no JUnit-recognized methods), so it doesn't break existing CI wiring — the meaningful verification is via the javac/java regression_commands provided.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-022 Zip Slip in zip4j by adding a centralized canonical-path containment check that rejects any archive-entry-derived output path that resolves outside the caller-supplied extraction root, before any mkdirs/delete/write happens.

commands_run: bash run_in_docker.sh "mkdir -p target/test-classes && javac -cp target/classes -d target/test-classes src/test/java/net/lingala/zip4j/ZipSlipRegressionTest.java && java -cp target/classes:target/test-classes net.lingala.zip4j.ZipSlipRegressionTest"
parsed_output.diff_review: patch_only.diff touches only 3 main-source files plus 1 new test file (build artifacts under target/ are incidental noise from a prior build, not functional changes). Zip4jUtil.checkPathIsContainedInRoot canonicalizes both the extraction root and the candidate output path via File#getCanonicalPath() and rejects any candidate that isn't the root or a canonical descendant, which correctly handles '../' traversal at any depth, absolute-path entries, mixed separators, and symlinked-root escapes (all called out in the exploiter's regression_hint). The check is centralized in getOutputFileNameWithPath, so it covers every caller (getOutputStream's mkdirs/delete/FileOutputStream sinks named in the alert, plus the applyFileAttributes call site at line 93 that the alert didn't separately trace but the exploiter flagged as same-class). The two added calls in Unzip.java close two sibling gaps (directory-entry extraction and pre-UnzipEngine parent-dir creation) that would otherwise still let an attacker create arbitrary directories even after the UnzipEngine fix — this is a justified, narrowly-scoped extension of the same fix, not unrelated behavior. The new ZipSlipRegressionTest.java is a plain (JUnit-free, matching the project's existing lack of a test framework) regression check exercising the traversal-file, traversal-directory, and normal-extraction cases; it does not touch or weaken the PoV. No vulnerable functionality was removed beyond the necessary traversal rejection; normal (non-traversal) extraction continues to work per the regression test's 'PASS' on checkNormalExtractionStillWorks.

parsed_output.summary: Patch adds a centralized canonical-path containment check (Zip4jUtil.checkPathIsContainedInRoot) invoked from UnzipEngine.getOutputFileNameWithPath (covering the getOutputStream write/mkdirs/delete sinks and the applyFileAttributes call site named in the alert) and from the two sibling unsanitized-path call sites in Unzip.java (directory-entry mkdirs and checkOutputDirectoryStructure's parent mkdirs). Any archive-entry-derived path that resolves outside the extraction root now throws ZipException before any filesystem mutation. Independently reran the PoV and regression commands via the docker wrapper against the patched worktree and confirmed the fix.
